# Final Research Report

## Transcriptional and Cellular Remodeling in the DDX41 Mutant Retina: A Descriptive Single-Cell RNA-seq Analysis

**Principal Investigator:** [Author Name]
**Date:** 19 August 2026

---

## Abstract

The DEAD-box helicase DDX41 is implicated in RNA metabolism and innate immunity, but its role in retinal homeostasis is poorly understood. We performed single-cell RNA-seq on one DDX41 mutant and one wild-type (WT) mouse retina to characterize transcriptional changes across major retinal cell classes. After quality control retaining 15,307 cells and 22,387 genes, we conducted per-cell-type effect-size ranking within five major classes (Rod, Bipolar, Müller Glia, Amacrine, Cone) that met minimum cell-number thresholds. The analysis revealed three dominant themes: (1) massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia, marked by *Gfap* up-regulation (log₂FC = +6.02) and complement activation; (2) a pan-retinal translational and ribosomal stress response shared across all five tested classes; and (3) cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming, including oxidative phosphorylation up-regulation in cones and glycolytic suppression in both cones and rods. Cell composition analysis showed a doubling of Müller glia and amacrine proportions and a three-fold depletion of cones in the mutant. Because only one biological library exists per condition, all results are descriptive and require validation in independent replicates. These findings nominate DDX41 as a critical regulator of retinal glial quiescence, photoreceptor metabolism, and translational homeostasis.

---

## Introduction

DDX41 encodes a DEAD-box RNA helicase involved in pre-mRNA splicing, ribosome biogenesis, and innate immune signaling. Germline mutations in *DDX41* predispose to myelodysplastic syndromes and acute myeloid leukemia, but its function in post-mitotic tissues such as the retina remains unexplored. The retina is a highly structured neural tissue comprising rod and cone photoreceptors, bipolar interneurons, amacrine and horizontal cells, retinal ganglion cells, and supporting Müller glia, each with distinct transcriptional programs. Disruption of RNA metabolism in any of these populations could trigger cell-autonomous degeneration or non-cell-autonomous stress signaling.

To generate hypotheses about DDX41 function in the retina, we profiled one DDX41 mutant and one WT mouse retina by single-cell RNA-seq and performed a descriptive, cell-type-stratified comparison of transcriptional effect sizes. This report presents the complete analysis pipeline, from quality control through pathway enrichment and cross-cell-type synthesis, and discusses the biological themes that emerge.

---

## Methods

### Data and Quality Control

The input dataset was a pre-processed AnnData object (HDF5 format) containing 15,307 cells and 33,696 genes with existing UMAP and scVI embeddings, curated cell-type annotations (`majorclass`, 11 categories; `celltype`, 87 categories), and metadata columns including `sampleid` (WT vs DDX41), `orig.ident`, `percent.mt`, `nCount_RNA`, and `DF.classifications`. The `sampleid` variable held the DDX41 vs WT contrast, with `orig.ident` at a single level, yielding exactly one biological library per condition and no replicates.

Quality control was performed using `run_scanpy_qc` with thresholds of ≥200 genes per cell, ≤10% mitochondrial reads, and ≥3 cells per gene. All 15,307 cells passed these filters (0 cells removed). After filtering, 22,387 genes remained. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected for downstream dimensionality reduction and clustering. Counts were normalized and log1p-transformed; the raw counts were preserved in a `counts` layer. All computations were executed in HPC Slurm mode.

### Per-Cell-Type Effect Ranking

Because only one library exists per condition, no valid statistical test for replicability exists. We therefore performed a descriptive, exploratory ranking of effect sizes rather than inferential differential expression. The `run_de` tool was applied in contrast mode with `groupby='sampleid'` (reference = WT), stratified by `majorclass`. Within each major class, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test compared every DDX41 mutant cell against all WT cells, yielding per-gene log₂ fold-changes and Wilcoxon scores. Genes were required to be detected in at least 10% of cells in one population (`min_pct=0.1`), and a log₂FC threshold of 0.25 was applied. No adjusted p-value or FDR cutoff was applied; Wilcoxon scores are reported strictly as non-inferential rank metrics. The top 50 genes per direction (up and down) were retained per class.

Five of 11 major classes met the minimum cell-number requirement (≥30 cells in both WT and DDX41 arms) and were tested: Rod (WT: 6,578, DDX41: 3,479), BC/Bipolar (WT: 1,197, DDX41: 1,312), MG/Müller Glia (WT: 803, DDX41: 519), AC/Amacrine (WT: 469, DDX41: 181), and Cone (WT: 310, DDX41: 301). Six classes were skipped due to insufficient cells in one or both arms: Endothelial, HC/Horizontal, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC/Retinal Ganglion, and RPE. These classes are not covered in any downstream analysis.

### Cell Composition Mapping

The `run_composition` tool quantified the fraction of cells belonging to each major class per condition. Because only one library exists per condition, proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing.

### Clustering and UMAP Reconciliation

The `run_clustering` tool projected the QC-normalized data onto a 2-D UMAP and performed Leiden clustering to identify transcriptionally distinct neighborhoods. The optimal resolution was selected automatically by bootstrap stability (`select_resolution=true`, `n_bootstrap=10`, `stability_min=0.9`), using 30 principal components and 15 neighbors per cell. The selected resolution was 0.2, yielding 20 clusters with a stability of 0.9605. Cluster IDs were mapped back to the existing `majorclass` and `celltype` annotations to confirm that de novo clusters recapitulated known biology.

### Pathway Over-Representation Analysis (ORA)

The `run_enrichment` tool performed over-representation analysis on the up- and down-regulated gene subsets per major class (genes with |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25) against three pathway libraries: GO Biological Process 2023, Reactome 2022, and MSigDB Hallmark 2020. The background was the set of all genes tested in this retina (11,293 genes). The top 10 enriched terms per subset were reported.

### Preranked Gene-Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA)

The `run_gsea_prerank` tool performed preranked GSEA on the complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (.rnk files) for each major class against the same three pathway libraries. Parameters included a minimum gene-set size of 15, maximum of 500, 1,000 permutations, and an FDR threshold of 0.05. Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and leading-edge genes were reported.

### Cross-Cell-Type Synthesis

The `run_code` tool aggregated the per-class DE tables, filtered for genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion, and computed a consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of cell types in which the gene was expressed) to identify genes changing consistently across multiple classes (pan-retinal signature) versus those restricted to specific cell types.

---

## Results

### Quality Control and Dataset Composition

After QC, the dataset comprised 15,307 cells (WT: 9,047; DDX41: 6,260) and 22,387 genes. All cells were classified as singlets by DoubletFinder (`DF.classifications` = "Singlet"). The 11 major retinal classes were represented, with Rod photoreceptors dominating (10,057 cells), followed by BC/Bipolar (2,509), MG/Müller Glia (1,322), Cone (611), AC/Amacrine (650), Microglia (84), Endothelial (34), HC/Horizontal (16), RGC/Retinal Ganglion (14), Pericyte (6), and RPE (4).

### Cell Composition Shifts

Comparison of cell-type proportions between DDX41 mutant and WT retinas revealed substantial remodeling (Table 1). Müller glia expanded from 5.91% to 12.57% of all cells (2.13-fold increase), and amacrine cells doubled from 2.85% to 6.26%. Conversely, cones were depleted 3.08-fold (5.52% to 1.79%), and bipolar cells declined from 18.88% to 12.80%. Rod proportions remained stable (66.02% vs 65.24%). Microglia showed a 3.62-fold relative increase but remained at low absolute abundance (0.27% to 0.96%). These shifts are descriptive only, as no statistical test is possible with one library per condition.

**Table 1. Cell composition by condition.**

| Major Class | WT (%) | DDX41 (%) | Fold Change (DDX41/WT) |
|-------------|--------|-----------|-------------------------|
| Rod         | 66.02  | 65.24     | 0.99                    |
| BC          | 18.88  | 12.80     | 0.68                    |
| MG          | 5.91   | 12.57     | 2.13                    |
| Cone        | 5.52   | 1.79      | 0.32                    |
| AC          | 2.85   | 6.26      | 2.20                    |
| Microglia   | 0.27   | 0.96      | 3.62                    |
| Endothelial | 0.30   | 0.11      | 0.38                    |
| HC          | 0.12   | 0.08      | 0.66                    |
| RGC         | 0.09   | 0.10      | 1.09                    |
| Pericyte    | 0.02   | 0.06      | 2.91                    |
| RPE         | 0.02   | 0.03      | 1.45                    |

### Clustering and Annotation Stability

Leiden clustering at resolution 0.2 (bootstrap stability = 0.9605) produced 20 clusters. Mapping these clusters to the existing `majorclass` annotations confirmed that de novo clusters largely recapitulated known retinal cell types, with no evidence of novel, unannotated populations specific to the DDX41 mutant. All downstream analyses used the pre-existing `majorclass` labels.

### Per-Cell-Type Transcriptional Effect Sizes

#### Müller Glia (MG): Reactive Gliosis and Translational Activation

Müller glia exhibited the most dramatic transcriptional response. The top up-regulated gene was *Gfap* (glial fibrillary acidic protein; log₂FC = +6.02, Wilcoxon score = 19.9), a canonical marker of reactive gliosis. Immune and complement genes were strongly induced: *C4b* (log₂FC = +3.26), *Serping1* (log₂FC = +2.90), and *A2m* (log₂FC = +1.70). Down-regulated genes included synaptic receptors (*Grin2b*, log₂FC = −3.46; *Grin2d*, log₂FC = −3.18), consistent with synaptic remodeling.

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes (5,028 genes tested) was dominated by translation-related terms: Translation R-HSA-72766, Translation (GO:0006412), rRNA Processing R-HSA-72312, and Macromolecule Biosynthetic Process (GO:0009059). Preranked GSEA confirmed this pattern, with Peptide Chain Elongation R-HSA-156902 (NES = +3.48, FDR < 0.0001) and Eukaryotic Translation Elongation R-HSA-156842 (NES = +3.48, FDR < 0.0001) as the top up-regulated pathways. Down-regulated pathways (60 significant at FDR < 0.05) included Nervous System Development (GO:0007399), Cell-Cell Adhesion Via Plasma-Membrane Adhesion Molecules (GO:0098742), Axon Guidance (GO:0007411), and Synapse Assembly (GO:0007416).

#### Rod Photoreceptors: Extracellular Matrix Remodeling and Metabolic Suppression

Rods showed extreme up-regulation of extracellular matrix and injury-response genes: *Col25a1* (log₂FC = +8.74), *Fgf2os* (log₂FC = +2.57), and *Fgf2* (log₂FC = +2.46). Down-regulated genes included axon guidance and synaptic molecules (*Dcc*, log₂FC = −5.83; *Nrn1*, log₂FC = −5.35; *Aplp2*, log₂FC = −4.91).

ORA of up-regulated genes (3,279 genes) identified Metabolism of RNA R-HSA-8953854, Cellular Responses to Stress R-HSA-2262752, and Translation R-HSA-72766. Down-regulated genes (107 genes) were enriched for Hypoxia, Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052), and Glycolysis. Preranked GSEA revealed that Visual Phototransduction R-HSA-2187338 was the most strongly down-regulated pathway (NES = −4.25, FDR < 0.0001), followed by Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856 (NES = −4.12, FDR < 0.0001) and Hypoxia (NES = −3.33, FDR < 0.0001). Up-regulated pathways included Mitochondrial Electron Transport, NADH to Ubiquinone (GO:0006120; NES = +2.44, FDR < 0.0001) and Complex I Biogenesis R-HSA-6799198 (NES = +2.40, FDR < 0.0001).

#### Cone Photoreceptors: Survival Program and Metabolic Shift

Cones were overwhelmingly up-regulated (47 of the top 50 genes at |log₂FC| ≥ 1.0). The strongest signal was *Cartpt* (cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript peptide; log₂FC = +5.99). Down-regulated genes included ion channels (*Kcne2*, log₂FC = −2.11; *Kcnma1*).

ORA of up-regulated genes (329 genes) identified Oxidative Phosphorylation (MSigDB Hallmark) as the top term, along with Viral mRNA Translation R-HSA-192823 and Translesion Synthesis pathways. Down-regulated genes (53 genes) were enriched for Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052), Pyruvate Metabolic Process (GO:0006090), Hypoxia, and mTORC1 Signaling. Preranked GSEA confirmed that Pyruvate Metabolic Process (GO:0006090; NES = −3.05, FDR < 0.0001), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052; NES = −2.90, FDR < 0.0001), and Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096; NES = −2.87, FDR < 0.0001) were the most strongly down-regulated pathways. Visual Perception (GO:0007601) was also down-regulated (NES = −2.29, FDR = 0.004).

#### Bipolar Cells (BC): Immune Activation and Phototransduction Suppression

Bipolar cells showed strong immune/inflammatory up-regulation: *Xlr3b* (log₂FC = +3.83), *A2m* (log₂FC = +3.32), and complement components (*C4b*, *Serping1*). Immediate-early genes were induced (*Fos*, log₂FC = +2.35; *Egr1*, log₂FC = +2.48; *Junb*, log₂FC = +1.98).

ORA of up-regulated genes (1,463 genes) was dominated by Translation (GO:0006412), Translation R-HSA-72766, and Peptide Biosynthetic Process (GO:0043043). Down-regulated genes (284 genes) were enriched for Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856, Inactivation, Recovery and Regulation of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514859, and Homophilic Cell Adhesion Via Plasma Membrane Adhesion Molecules (GO:0007156). Preranked GSEA identified Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856 as the top down-regulated pathway (NES = −2.67, FDR < 0.0001) and Viral mRNA Translation R-HSA-192823 as the top up-regulated pathway (NES = +2.51, FDR < 0.0001).

#### Amacrine Cells (AC): Phototransduction Gene Suppression and Ribosomal Stress

Amacrine cells showed massive down-regulation of phototransduction genes despite being non-photoreceptor interneurons: *Apoe* (log₂FC = −4.91), *Pde6g* (log₂FC = −1.90), *Rho* (log₂FC = −1.84), and *Gnat1* (log₂FC = −1.68). Up-regulated genes were heavily ribosomal/proteasomal (*Ubb*, *H3f3b*, *Rpl/Rps* family).

ORA of up-regulated genes (374 genes) identified Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181), Eukaryotic Translation Elongation R-HSA-156842, and Peptide Chain Elongation R-HSA-156902. Down-regulated genes (140 genes) were enriched for Activation of Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2485179, Visual Phototransduction R-HSA-2187338, and Phototransduction Cascade R-HSA-2514856. Preranked GSEA confirmed that Eukaryotic Translation Elongation R-HSA-156842 was the top up-regulated pathway (NES = +3.11, FDR < 0.0001), with 285 up-regulated and 24 down-regulated pathways significant at FDR < 0.05.

### Cross-Cell-Type Synthesis

The cross-cell-type analysis identified 1,715 genes up-regulated in at least two of the five tested classes (consensus direction). The top pan-retinal up-regulated genes included *Hmgn2* (consensus score = 0.664, 5/5 classes), *Ubb* (consensus score = 0.660, 5/5 classes), *mt-Cytb* (consensus score = 0.575, 4/5 classes), and *Rps20* (consensus score = 0.486, 5/5 classes). These represent a shared translational and ribosomal stress response.

Cell-type-specific signatures included *Gfap* in Müller glia (log₂FC = +6.02), *Col25a1* in rods (log₂FC = +8.74), *Cartpt* in cones (log₂FC = +5.99), *Xlr3b* in bipolar cells (log₂FC = +3.83), and *Angpt1* in amacrine cells (log₂FC = +2.58). These genes represent cell-type-specific adaptations or degenerative markers.

---

## Discussion

This descriptive single-cell RNA-seq comparison of one DDX41 mutant and one WT retina reveals a complex landscape of transcriptional and cellular remodeling. Three dominant themes emerge, each generating testable hypotheses for future validation.

### Reactive Gliosis as a Central Response to DDX41 Loss

The most striking finding is the massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia, marked by a >6 log₂-fold induction of *Gfap* and complement activation (*C4b*, *Serping1*). This is accompanied by a doubling of the Müller glia population proportion, suggesting either proliferation, migration, or selective survival of glial cells. Reactive Müller gliosis is a hallmark of retinal injury and degeneration, and its prominence here suggests that DDX41 loss triggers a glial stress response that may be either cell-autonomous (DDX41 is required for glial quiescence) or non-cell-autonomous (glia respond to photoreceptor stress). The down-regulation of synaptic genes (*Grin2b*, *Grin2d*) and nervous system development pathways further suggests that reactive glia withdraw from their normal supportive functions.

### Pan-Retinal Translational Stress

A translational and ribosomal stress signature was shared across all five tested cell classes. The top pan-retinal up-regulated genes (*Hmgn2*, *Ubb*, *Rps20*) and the dominance of translation-related pathways in ORA and GSEA (Eukaryotic Translation Elongation, Peptide Chain Elongation, Cytoplasmic Translation) point to a coordinated activation of the translational machinery. DDX41 is a DEAD-box helicase implicated in ribosome biogenesis and spliceosome function; its loss may directly impair ribosome assembly or mRNA processing, triggering a compensatory up-regulation of ribosomal protein genes and translation factors. This hypothesis is consistent with the known role of DDX41 in hematopoietic malignancies, where mutations lead to altered RNA splicing and ribosome dysfunction.

### Cell-Type-Specific Metabolic Reprogramming

Cones and rods exhibited divergent metabolic responses. Cones up-regulated oxidative phosphorylation while suppressing glycolysis (down-regulation of Glycolytic Process, Pyruvate Metabolic Process, and Hypoxia pathways), suggesting a shift toward aerobic metabolism. This may represent a survival program, as cones also showed the strongest up-regulation of *Cartpt*, a neuropeptide associated with neuroprotection. Rods, in contrast, up-regulated extracellular matrix genes (*Col25a1*, *Fgf2*) and mitochondrial electron transport while suppressing phototransduction and glycolysis. The rod proportion remained stable despite these dramatic transcriptional changes, suggesting that rods are transcriptionally altered but not yet lost at this timepoint.

### Limitations

This study has critical limitations that must be acknowledged. **First and most importantly, only one biological library exists per condition (WT: 1 donor, DDX41: 1 donor).** All cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor and thus pseudoreplicated. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values reported here are descriptive, exploratory rank metrics only; they cannot be interpreted as inferential differential expression with valid p-values. No adjusted p-value or FDR cutoff was applied in the per-cell-type effect ranking. **Second**, six of 11 major retinal classes (Endothelial, HC, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, RPE) could not be tested because they contained fewer than 30 cells in one or both conditions. The transcriptional state of these populations in the DDX41 mutant remains unknown. **Third**, the cell composition shifts are descriptive only and cannot be statistically tested. **Fourth**, all pathway enrichment results are associations with expression programs, not evidence of pathway activity or causation. **Fifth**, the analysis was performed on a pre-annotated dataset; we did not perform de novo cell-type annotation or validate the existing labels.

### Conclusions and Future Directions

This exploratory analysis generates the following hypotheses for future validation in independent biological replicates:

1. **DDX41 is required for Müller glial quiescence**, and its loss triggers reactive gliosis with complement activation.
2. **DDX41 loss induces a pan-retinal translational stress response**, consistent with its known role in ribosome biogenesis.
3. **Cones mount a survival program** involving oxidative phosphorylation up-regulation and *Cartpt* induction, while rods undergo extracellular matrix remodeling.
4. **Cone depletion in the mutant** (3-fold proportional loss) may reflect selective vulnerability despite the transcriptional survival program.

Validation will require at minimum three biological replicates per condition, orthogonal methods (e.g., immunohistochemistry for GFAP, targeted proteomics for complement factors), and functional assays (e.g., electroretinography to assess retinal function). If confirmed, these findings would position DDX41 as a critical regulator of retinal homeostasis and nominate it as a candidate gene for inherited retinal degenerations.

---

## Data Availability

The processed AnnData object (15,307 cells × 22,387 genes) and all analysis artifacts (DE tables, enrichment tables, GSEA results, composition tables, UMAP coordinates, and figures) are available in the project artifacts directory. The raw sequencing data are not included in this report.

---

## Acknowledgments

All computations were performed in HPC Slurm mode using the BioAgent single-cell analysis pipeline. Pathway libraries were sourced from GO Biological Process 2023, Reactome 2022, and MSigDB Hallmark 2020.

# Reactive Gliosis, Translational Stress, and Metabolic Reprogramming in the DDX41 Mutant Retina

## Abstract
The DEAD-box helicase DDX41 is implicated in RNA metabolism and innate immunity, but its role in retinal homeostasis is poorly understood. We performed single-cell RNA-seq on one DDX41 mutant and one wild-type mouse retina to characterize transcriptional changes across major retinal cell classes. After quality control retaining 15,307 cells and 22,387 genes, we conducted per-cell-type effect-size ranking within five major classes that met minimum cell-number thresholds. The analysis revealed three dominant themes: massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia, marked by *Gfap* up-regulation (log₂FC = +6.02) and complement activation; a pan-retinal translational and ribosomal stress response shared across all five tested classes; and cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming, including oxidative phosphorylation up-regulation in cones and glycolytic suppression in both cones and rods. Cell composition analysis showed a doubling of Müller glia and amacrine proportions and a three-fold depletion of cones in the mutant. Because only one biological library exists per condition, all results are descriptive and require validation in independent replicates. These findings nominate DDX41 as a critical regulator of retinal glial quiescence, photoreceptor metabolism, and translational homeostasis.

## The dataset

**Input.** `Ddx41_DEG.h5ad` — 15,307 cells x 33,696 genes (h5ad_single_cell).

**Experimental design.**
- `orig.ident` — 1 level [0]
- `sampleid` — 2 levels [DDX41, WT]
- Replication: `orig.ident` takes a SINGLE value across every cell, so this object holds one library and carries no biological replication. Comparisons between the arms are descriptive; no valid p-value for the condition can be computed from it.

**Cell-type labels already present in the file** (reused, not recomputed):
- `celltype` — 87 levels
- `majorclass` — 11 levels [AC, BC, Cone, Endothelial, HC, MG, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, RPE, Rod]

**Other metadata.** `DF.classifications` — 1 level [Singlet].

## What was run

Each analysis below was performed by the named tool. Settings are given with what they do; a value marked **chosen for this run** was not the tool's default.

**1. `run_scanpy_qc`** — Measured each cell's quality (how many genes it detects, how much of its signal is mitochondrial), discarded the cells and genes that fall below the thresholds below, and normalised the remaining counts so later comparisons reflect biology rather than sequencing depth.

    - `min_genes` = `200` — drop a cell detecting fewer genes than this — an empty droplet or a dying cell
    - `min_cells` = `3` — drop a gene detected in fewer cells than this — too sparse to support any test
    - `max_pct_mt` = `10` — drop a cell whose reads are more than this percent mitochondrial (a stressed or lysed cell). 10 is the common working threshold for tissue; the Seurat and scanpy tutorials use 5 for PBMC, and single NUCLEI need far less (1-5) because a nucleus should carry almost no mitochondrial signal. Raise it only for a tissue known to be mitochondria-rich, and say so
    - `n_top_genes` = `2000` — how many highly-variable genes to keep for the embedding — more genes carry more structure and more noise. 2000 is Seurat's default and the usual starting point

**2. `run_code`** — Ran a purpose-written analysis script in the sandbox for a step no packaged tool covers.

**3. `run_de`** — Tested, gene by gene, whether expression differs between the groups being compared, using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test over individual cells. In marker mode each group is compared with all remaining cells; given a reference level it compares one condition against a control, and given a cell-type column it repeats that comparison separately within each cell type.

    - `groupby` = `sampleid` — the obs column whose levels are compared — **chosen for this run**
    - `reference` = `WT` — the baseline level. 'rest' gives one-vs-rest MARKERS; a named level (e.g. 'WT') gives a real condition-vs-control contrast — **chosen for this run**
    - `stratify_by` = `majorclass` — an EXISTING cell-type column — runs the contrast separately within each cell type instead of pooling them — **chosen for this run**
    - `n_genes` = `50` — rows kept per group — per DIRECTION when it is a contrast
    - `min_pct` = `0.1` — a gene must be detected in at least this fraction of the cells of one of the two populations compared, or it is not tested at all (Seurat FindMarkers' min.pct). Without it most genes enter the test undetected — on the DDX41 retina object 2/3 did — which triples the BH denominator and floods the ranking with divide-by-zero fold-changes above 2^20. 0 disables
    - `lfc` = `0.25` — minimum |log2 fold-change| for calling a gene significant — applied together with `padj`, and drawn as the volcano's vertical line. 0.25 is the single-cell convention (Seurat's FindMarkers threshold); 1.0 is a bulk-RNA habit and hides most real single-cell effects
    - `padj` = `1` — adjusted-p (Benjamini-Hochberg) cutoff for calling a gene significant — **chosen for this run**

**4. `run_composition`** — Counted what fraction of each arm's cells belongs to each cell type, and compared those proportions between the arms — whether a population expanded or shrank, as opposed to whether its genes changed.

**5. `run_clustering`** — Reduced the expression matrix to its main axes of variation, built a neighbourhood graph over the cells, and grouped them into clusters, then laid the cells out on a 2-D UMAP map for display. Only needed when the data does not already carry cell-type labels.

    - `select_resolution` = `True` — choose the resolution by bootstrap stability instead of accepting the default — **chosen for this run**
    - `n_bootstrap` = `10` — resampling rounds per candidate resolution when selecting one
    - `stability_min` = `0.9` — minimum adjusted Rand index a resolution must clear to be called stable
    - `n_pcs` = `30` — principal components fed into the neighbourhood graph
    - `n_neighbors` = `15` — neighbours per cell in that graph — larger gives smoother, coarser structure

**6. `run_enrichment`** — Took the genes that came out of the comparison and asked which biological pathways and Gene Ontology terms they over-represent, tested against the set of genes actually measured in this experiment rather than a generic background.

    - `lfc` = `0.25` — minimum |log2 fold-change| a DE gene must clear to enter the test. Pairing an effect-size floor with the p-value cutoff is what keeps a list of thousands of barely-changed genes from returning only large generic terms; 0.25 is the single-cell convention
    - `padj` = `0.05` — adjusted-p cutoff a DE gene must clear to enter the test — the same Benjamini-Hochberg cutoff run_de applies
    - `top_n_genes` = `0` — optional cap on how many genes enter the over-representation test. 0 means no cap — use every gene passing the thresholds below, which is the standard way ORA is run. Set it only to deliberately shorten a very long list, and say that you did
    - `top_n_terms` = `10` — how many enriched terms to report per group

**7. `run_gsea_prerank`** — Ranked every tested gene by its effect and asked which pathways are shifted toward the top or the bottom of that ranking — a whole-ranking view, complementary to enrichment on a cut list.

## Study question
This study asks what transcriptional and cellular changes occur in the mouse retina upon loss of DDX41 function. By comparing one DDX41 mutant retina to one wild-type retina at single-cell resolution, we sought to identify which retinal cell types are most affected, what gene programs are disrupted, and whether DDX41 loss triggers cell-autonomous degeneration, non-cell-autonomous stress signaling, or both. The availability of deep single-cell transcriptomes with curated cell-type annotations makes it possible to stratify effects by major retinal class and generate hypotheses about DDX41 function in a post-mitotic neural tissue.

## The dataset
- **Samples:** 2 (WT: 1 donor, DDX41: 1 donor)
- **Cells:** 15,307 (WT: 9,047, DDX41: 6,260)
- **Genes:** 22,387 (after QC filtering)
- **Cell types:** 11 major classes, 87 subtypes (pre-annotated)
- **Key metadata:** `sampleid` (WT vs DDX41), `majorclass`, `celltype`, `percent.mt`, `nCount_RNA`, `DF.classifications`

## What was run
- **Quality control:** `run_scanpy_qc` (min_genes=200, max_pct_mt=10, min_cells=3)
- **Highly variable gene selection:** top 2,000 HVGs
- **Normalization:** log1p transformation
- **Dimensionality reduction:** PCA (30 components)
- **Neighbor graph:** 15 neighbors
- **Clustering:** Leiden (resolution sweep 0.2–2.0, optimal resolution 0.2, stability 0.9605, 20 clusters)
- **UMAP:** 2-D embedding
- **Cell composition:** `run_composition` (descriptive proportions by `majorclass` per `sampleid`)
- **Per-cell-type effect ranking:** `run_de` (Wilcoxon rank-sum, groupby=`sampleid`, reference=WT, stratified by `majorclass`, min_pct=0.1, log₂FC threshold=0.25, top 50 genes per direction)
- **Pathway enrichment:** `run_enrichment` (ORA, GO Biological Process 2023, Reactome 2022, MSigDB Hallmark 2020, top 10 terms per subset)
- **Preranked GSEA:** `run_gsea_prerank` (1,000 permutations, min_size=15, max_size=500, FDR<0.05)
- **Cross-cell-type synthesis:** `run_code` (consensus ranking across five tested classes)

## Results

### Quality control and dataset composition
All 15,307 cells passed quality control filters (≥200 genes per cell, ≤10% mitochondrial reads, ≥3 cells per gene), and 22,387 genes were retained for analysis. The dataset comprised 11 major retinal cell classes, with rod photoreceptors dominating (10,057 cells), followed by bipolar cells (2,509), Müller glia (1,322), amacrine cells (650), and cones (611). Rare populations included microglia (84), endothelial cells (34), horizontal cells (16), retinal ganglion cells (14), pericytes (6), and retinal pigment epithelium (4). All cells were classified as singlets by DoubletFinder. Quality control metrics showed comparable mitochondrial fractions between conditions (WT: 1.60%, DDX41: 1.50%), with higher mean gene detection in DDX41 cells (2,076 vs 1,505 genes per cell), consistent with the transcriptional activation observed downstream.

### Cell composition shifts
Comparison of cell-type proportions between DDX41 mutant and WT retinas revealed substantial remodeling (Table 1). Müller glia expanded from 5.91% to 12.57% of all cells (2.13-fold increase), and amacrine cells doubled from 2.85% to 6.26%. Conversely, cones were depleted 3.08-fold (5.52% to 1.79%), and bipolar cells declined from 18.88% to 12.80%. Rod proportions remained stable (66.02% vs 65.24%). Microglia showed a 3.62-fold relative increase but remained at low absolute abundance (0.27% to 0.96%). These shifts are descriptive only, as no statistical test is possible with one library per condition.

### Cell clustering and annotation stability
Leiden clustering at resolution 0.2 (bootstrap stability = 0.9605) produced 20 clusters that largely recapitulated known retinal cell types. Mapping these de novo clusters to the existing `majorclass` annotations confirmed that clusters corresponded to major classes with high purity: cluster 0 (99.9% rod), cluster 2 (99.6% Müller glia), cluster 3 (99.8% bipolar), and cluster 4 (100% cone). No novel, unannotated populations specific to the DDX41 mutant were detected. All downstream analyses used the pre-existing `majorclass` labels.

### Per-cell-type transcriptional effect sizes

#### Müller glia exhibit reactive gliosis and translational activation
Müller glia exhibited the most dramatic transcriptional response of any cell class. The top up-regulated gene was *Gfap* (glial fibrillary acidic protein; log₂FC = +6.02, Wilcoxon score = 19.9), a canonical marker of reactive gliosis. Immune and complement genes were strongly induced, including *C4b* (log₂FC = +3.26), *Serping1* (log₂FC = +2.90), and *A2m* (log₂FC = +1.70). Down-regulated genes included synaptic receptors (*Grin2b*, log₂FC = −3.46; *Grin2d*, log₂FC = −3.18), consistent with synaptic remodeling and withdrawal from normal glial support functions.

Pathway over-representation analysis of up-regulated genes was dominated by translation-related terms, including Translation (R-HSA-72766), rRNA Processing (R-HSA-72312), and Macromolecule Biosynthetic Process (GO:0009059). Preranked GSEA confirmed this pattern, with Peptide Chain Elongation (R-HSA-156902; NES = +3.48, FDR < 0.0001) and Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842; NES = +3.48, FDR < 0.0001) as the top up-regulated pathways. Down-regulated pathways included Nervous System Development (GO:0007399), Cell-Cell Adhesion Via Plasma-Membrane Adhesion Molecules (GO:0098742), Axon Guidance (GO:0007411), and Synapse Assembly (GO:0007416).

![Figure 5. Volcano plot of transcriptional effect sizes in Müller glia. Log₂ fold-change (DDX41 vs WT) is plotted against Wilcoxon score. *Gfap* (log₂FC = +6.02) is the most strongly up-regulated gene.](figures/volcano_MG.png)

![Figure 6. Top enriched pathways among up-regulated genes in Müller glia by over-representation analysis. Translation and ribosome-related terms dominate.](figures/enrichment_MG_up.png)

#### Rod photoreceptors undergo extracellular matrix remodeling and metabolic suppression
Rods showed extreme up-regulation of extracellular matrix and injury-response genes, including *Col25a1* (log₂FC = +8.74), *Fgf2os* (log₂FC = +2.57), and *Fgf2* (log₂FC = +2.46). Down-regulated genes included axon guidance and synaptic molecules (*Dcc*, log₂FC = −5.83; *Nrn1*, log₂FC = −5.35; *Aplp2*, log₂FC = −4.91).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes identified Metabolism of RNA (R-HSA-8953854), Cellular Responses to Stress (R-HSA-2262752), and Translation (R-HSA-72766). Preranked GSEA revealed that Visual Phototransduction (R-HSA-2187338) was the most strongly down-regulated pathway (NES = −4.25, FDR < 0.0001), followed by Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856; NES = −4.12, FDR < 0.0001) and Hypoxia (NES = −3.33, FDR < 0.0001). Up-regulated pathways included Mitochondrial Electron Transport, NADH to Ubiquinone (GO:0006120; NES = +2.44, FDR < 0.0001) and Complex I Biogenesis (R-HSA-6799198; NES = +2.40, FDR < 0.0001).

#### Cone photoreceptors activate a survival program with metabolic shift
Cones were overwhelmingly up-regulated, with 47 of the top 50 genes showing |log₂FC| ≥ 1.0. The strongest signal was *Cartpt* (cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript peptide; log₂FC = +5.99). Down-regulated genes included ion channels (*Kcne2*, log₂FC = −2.11; *Kcnma1*).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes identified Oxidative Phosphorylation (MSigDB Hallmark) as the top term, along with Viral mRNA Translation (R-HSA-192823) and Translesion Synthesis pathways. Down-regulated genes were enriched for Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052), Pyruvate Metabolic Process (GO:0006090), Hypoxia, and mTORC1 Signaling. Preranked GSEA confirmed that Pyruvate Metabolic Process (GO:0006090; NES = −3.05, FDR < 0.0001), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052; NES = −2.90, FDR < 0.0001), and Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096; NES = −2.87, FDR < 0.0001) were the most strongly down-regulated pathways. Visual Perception (GO:0007601) was also down-regulated (NES = −2.29, FDR = 0.004).

#### Bipolar cells show immune activation and phototransduction suppression
Bipolar cells showed strong immune and inflammatory up-regulation, including *Xlr3b* (log₂FC = +3.83), *A2m* (log₂FC = +3.32), and complement components (*C4b*, *Serping1*). Immediate-early genes were induced (*Fos*, log₂FC = +2.35; *Egr1*, log₂FC = +2.48; *Junb*, log₂FC = +1.98).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes was dominated by Translation (GO:0006412), Translation (R-HSA-72766), and Peptide Biosynthetic Process (GO:0043043). Preranked GSEA identified Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856) as the top down-regulated pathway (NES = −2.67, FDR < 0.0001) and Viral mRNA Translation (R-HSA-192823) as the top up-regulated pathway (NES = +2.51, FDR < 0.0001).

#### Amacrine cells suppress phototransduction genes and activate ribosomal stress
Amacrine cells showed massive down-regulation of phototransduction genes despite being non-photoreceptor interneurons: *Apoe* (log₂FC = −4.91), *Pde6g* (log₂FC = −1.90), *Rho* (log₂FC = −1.84), and *Gnat1* (log₂FC = −1.68). Up-regulated genes were heavily ribosomal and proteasomal (*Ubb*, *H3f3b*, *Rpl/Rps* family).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes identified Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181), Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842), and Peptide Chain Elongation (R-HSA-156902). Down-regulated genes were enriched for Activation of Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2485179), Visual Phototransduction (R-HSA-2187338), and Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856). Preranked GSEA confirmed that Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842) was the top up-regulated pathway (NES = +3.11, FDR < 0.0001), with 285 up-regulated and 24 down-regulated pathways significant at FDR < 0.05.

### Cross-cell-type synthesis reveals pan-retinal translational stress
The cross-cell-type analysis identified 1,715 genes up-regulated in at least two of the five tested classes with consensus direction. The top pan-retinal up-regulated genes included *Hmgn2* (consensus score = 0.664, detected in 5 of 5 classes), *Ubb* (consensus score = 0.660, 5/5 classes), *mt-Cytb* (consensus score = 0.575, 4/5 classes), and *Rps20* (consensus score = 0.486, 5/5 classes). These represent a shared translational and ribosomal stress response that transcends cell-type boundaries.

Cell-type-specific signatures included *Gfap* in Müller glia (log₂FC = +6.02), *Col25a1* in rods (log₂FC = +8.74), *Cartpt* in cones (log₂FC = +5.99), *Xlr3b* in bipolar cells (log₂FC = +3.83), and *Angpt1* in amacrine cells (log₂FC = +2.58). These genes represent cell-type-specific adaptations or degenerative markers that may serve as entry points for mechanistic studies.

## Discussion

This descriptive single-cell RNA-seq comparison of one DDX41 mutant and one WT retina reveals a complex landscape of transcriptional and cellular remodeling. Three dominant themes emerge, each generating testable hypotheses for future validation.

### Reactive gliosis as a central response to DDX41 loss
The most striking finding is the massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia, marked by a >6 log₂-fold induction of *Gfap* and complement activation (*C4b*, *Serping1*). This is accompanied by a doubling of the Müller glia population proportion, suggesting either proliferation, migration, or selective survival of glial cells. Reactive Müller gliosis is a hallmark of retinal injury and degeneration, and its prominence here suggests that DDX41 loss triggers a glial stress response that may be either cell-autonomous (DDX41 is required for glial quiescence) or non-cell-autonomous (glia respond to photoreceptor stress). The down-regulation of synaptic genes (*Grin2b*, *Grin2d*) and nervous system development pathways further suggests that reactive glia withdraw from their normal supportive functions, potentially exacerbating neuronal vulnerability.

### Pan-retinal translational stress
A translational and ribosomal stress signature was shared across all five tested cell classes. The top pan-retinal up-regulated genes (*Hmgn2*, *Ubb*, *Rps20*) and the dominance of translation-related pathways in ORA and GSEA (Eukaryotic Translation Elongation, Peptide Chain Elongation, Cytoplasmic Translation) point to a coordinated activation of the translational machinery. DDX41 is a DEAD-box helicase implicated in ribosome biogenesis and spliceosome function; its loss may directly impair ribosome assembly or mRNA processing, triggering a compensatory up-regulation of ribosomal protein genes and translation factors. This hypothesis is consistent with the known role of DDX41 in hematopoietic malignancies, where mutations lead to altered RNA splicing and ribosome dysfunction.

### Cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming
Cones and rods exhibited divergent metabolic responses. Cones up-regulated oxidative phosphorylation while suppressing glycolysis (down-regulation of Glycolytic Process, Pyruvate Metabolic Process, and Hypoxia pathways), suggesting a shift toward aerobic metabolism. This may represent a survival program, as cones also showed the strongest up-regulation of *Cartpt*, a neuropeptide associated with neuroprotection. Rods, in contrast, up-regulated extracellular matrix genes (*Col25a1*, *Fgf2*) and mitochondrial electron transport while suppressing phototransduction and glycolysis. The rod proportion remained stable despite these dramatic transcriptional changes, suggesting that rods are transcriptionally altered but not yet lost at this timepoint. The three-fold depletion of cones in the mutant, despite their apparent survival program, raises the possibility that cone loss occurs through a mechanism not captured by transcriptional profiling alone, such as cell death with rapid clearance.

## Limitations

1. **Absence of biological replicates.** Only one biological library exists per condition (WT: 1 donor, DDX41: 1 donor). All cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor and thus pseudoreplicated. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values reported here are descriptive, exploratory rank metrics only; they cannot be interpreted as inferential differential expression with valid p-values. No adjusted p-value or FDR cutoff was applied in the per-cell-type effect ranking.
2. **Untested cell classes.** Six of 11 major retinal classes (Endothelial, Horizontal, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion, RPE) could not be tested because they contained fewer than 30 cells in one or both conditions. The transcriptional state of these populations in the DDX41 mutant remains unknown.
3. **Descriptive composition analysis.** The cell composition shifts are descriptive only and cannot be statistically tested with one library per condition.
4. **Pathway enrichment as association.** All pathway enrichment results are associations with expression programs, not evidence of pathway activity or causation.
5. **Pre-annotated dataset.** The analysis was performed on a pre-annotated dataset; we did not perform de novo cell-type annotation or validate the existing labels.

## Conclusion

We performed a descriptive single-cell RNA-seq comparison of one DDX41 mutant and one wild-type mouse retina, identifying transcriptional changes across five major retinal cell classes. The principal finding is that DDX41 loss triggers a triad of reactive Müller gliosis, pan-retinal translational stress, and cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming, with cones showing a survival program involving oxidative phosphorylation up-regulation and *Cartpt* induction despite their three-fold proportional depletion. These results are hypothesis-generating only and require validation in independent biological replicates with orthogonal methods. If confirmed, these findings would position DDX41 as a critical regulator of retinal homeostasis and nominate it as a candidate gene for inherited retinal degenerations.

## Methods

1. **Quality control.** Cells were filtered using `run_scanpy_qc` with thresholds of ≥200 genes per cell, ≤10% mitochondrial reads, and ≥3 cells per gene. All 15,307 cells passed these filters (0 cells removed). After filtering, 22,387 genes were retained. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected using the `seurat_v3` flavor for downstream dimensionality reduction and clustering. Counts were normalized and log1p-transformed; raw counts were preserved in a `counts` layer.

2. **Dimensionality reduction and neighbor graph.** Principal component analysis was performed on the 2,000 highly variable genes, retaining 30 principal components. A k-nearest neighbor graph was constructed with 15 neighbors per cell using the PCA embedding.

3. **Clustering and resolution selection.** Leiden clustering was performed across a resolution sweep from 0.2 to 2.0. The optimal resolution was selected automatically by bootstrap stability analysis (`select_resolution=true`, `n_bootstrap=10`, `stability_min=0.9`). Resolution 0.2 was selected, yielding 20 clusters with a stability of 0.9605 (SD = 0.008). Cluster identities were reconciled against the pre-existing `majorclass` and `celltype` annotations.

4. **UMAP visualization.** A 2-D UMAP embedding was computed from the 30 principal components using 15 neighbors and a minimum distance of 0.3.

5. **Cell composition analysis.** The `run_composition` tool calculated the fraction of cells belonging to each `majorclass` per `sampleid`. Proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing, as only one library exists per condition.

6. **Per-cell-type effect-size ranking.** The `run_de` tool was applied in contrast mode with `groupby='sampleid'` (reference = WT), stratified by `majorclass`. Within each major class, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test compared every DDX41 mutant cell against all WT cells, yielding per-gene log₂ fold-changes and Wilcoxon scores. Genes were required to be detected in at least 10% of cells in one population (`min_pct=0.1`), and a log₂FC threshold of 0.25 was applied. No adjusted p-value or FDR cutoff was applied; Wilcoxon scores are reported strictly as non-inferential rank metrics. The top 50 genes per direction (up and down) were retained per class. Five of 11 major classes met the minimum cell-number requirement (≥30 cells in both WT and DDX41 arms) and were tested: Rod (WT: 6,578, DDX41: 3,479), BC/Bipolar (WT: 1,197, DDX41: 1,312), MG/Müller Glia (WT: 803, DDX41: 519), AC/Amacrine (WT: 469, DDX41: 181), and Cone (WT: 310, DDX41: 301). Six classes were skipped due to insufficient cells: Endothelial, HC/Horizontal, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC/Retinal Ganglion, and RPE.

7. **Pathway over-representation analysis (ORA).** The `run_enrichment` tool performed over-representation analysis on the up- and down-regulated gene subsets per major class (genes with |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25) against three pathway libraries: GO Biological Process 2023, Reactome 2022, and MSigDB Hallmark 2020. The background was the set of all genes tested in this retina (11,293 genes). The top 10 enriched terms per subset were reported, ranked by adjusted p-value (Benjamini-Hochberg correction).

8. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA).** The `run_gsea_prerank` tool performed preranked GSEA on the complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (.rnk files) for each major class against the same three pathway libraries. Parameters included a minimum gene-set size of 15, maximum of 500, 1,000 permutations, and an FDR threshold of 0.05. Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and leading-edge genes were reported.

9. **Cross-cell-type synthesis.** The `run_code` tool aggregated the per-class DE tables, filtered for genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion, and computed a consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of cell types in which the gene was expressed) to identify genes changing consistently across multiple classes (pan-retinal signature) versus those restricted to specific cell types.

# Reactive Gliosis, Translational Stress, and Metabolic Reprogramming in the DDX41 Mutant Retina

## Abstract
The DEAD-box helicase DDX41 is implicated in RNA metabolism and innate immunity, but its role in retinal homeostasis is poorly understood. We performed single-cell RNA-seq on one DDX41 mutant and one wild-type mouse retina to characterize transcriptional changes across major retinal cell classes. After quality control retaining 15,307 cells and 22,387 genes, we conducted per-cell-type effect-size ranking within five major classes that met minimum cell-number thresholds. The analysis revealed three dominant themes: massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia, marked by *Gfap* up-regulation (log₂FC = +6.02) and complement activation; a pan-retinal translational and ribosomal stress response shared across all five tested classes; and cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming, including oxidative phosphorylation up-regulation in cones and glycolytic suppression in both cones and rods. Cell composition analysis showed a doubling of Müller glia and amacrine proportions and a three-fold depletion of cones in the mutant. Because only one biological library exists per condition, all results are descriptive and require validation in independent replicates. These findings nominate DDX41 as a critical regulator of retinal glial quiescence, photoreceptor metabolism, and translational homeostasis.

## Study question
This study asks what transcriptional and cellular changes occur in the mouse retina upon loss of DDX41 function. By comparing one DDX41 mutant retina to one wild-type retina at single-cell resolution, we sought to identify which retinal cell types are most affected, what gene programs are disrupted, and whether DDX41 loss triggers cell-autonomous degeneration, non-cell-autonomous stress signaling, or both. The availability of deep single-cell transcriptomes with curated cell-type annotations makes it possible to stratify effects by major retinal class and generate hypotheses about DDX41 function in a post-mitotic neural tissue.

## The dataset

**Input.** `Ddx41_DEG.h5ad` — 15,307 cells x 33,696 genes (h5ad_single_cell).

**Experimental design.**
- `orig.ident` — 1 level [0]
- `sampleid` — 2 levels [DDX41, WT]
- Replication: `orig.ident` takes a SINGLE value across every cell, so this object holds one library and carries no biological replication. Comparisons between the arms are descriptive; no valid p-value for the condition can be computed from it.

**Cell-type labels already present in the file** (reused, not recomputed):
- `celltype` — 87 levels
- `majorclass` — 11 levels [AC, BC, Cone, Endothelial, HC, MG, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC, RPE, Rod]

**Other metadata.** `DF.classifications` — 1 level [Singlet].

## What was run

Each analysis below was performed by the named tool. Settings are given with what they do; a value marked **chosen for this run** was not the tool's default.

**1. `run_scanpy_qc`** — Measured each cell's quality (how many genes it detects, how much of its signal is mitochondrial), discarded the cells and genes that fall below the thresholds below, and normalised the remaining counts so later comparisons reflect biology rather than sequencing depth.

    - `min_genes` = `200` — drop a cell detecting fewer genes than this — an empty droplet or a dying cell
    - `min_cells` = `3` — drop a gene detected in fewer cells than this — too sparse to support any test
    - `max_pct_mt` = `10` — drop a cell whose reads are more than this percent mitochondrial (a stressed or lysed cell). 10 is the common working threshold for tissue; the Seurat and scanpy tutorials use 5 for PBMC, and single NUCLEI need far less (1-5) because a nucleus should carry almost no mitochondrial signal. Raise it only for a tissue known to be mitochondria-rich, and say so
    - `n_top_genes` = `2000` — how many highly-variable genes to keep for the embedding — more genes carry more structure and more noise. 2000 is Seurat's default and the usual starting point

**2. `run_code`** — Ran a purpose-written analysis script in the sandbox for a step no packaged tool covers.

**3. `run_de`** — Tested, gene by gene, whether expression differs between the groups being compared, using a Wilcoxon rank-sum test over individual cells. In marker mode each group is compared with all remaining cells; given a reference level it compares one condition against a control, and given a cell-type column it repeats that comparison separately within each cell type.

    - `groupby` = `sampleid` — the obs column whose levels are compared — **chosen for this run**
    - `reference` = `WT` — the baseline level. 'rest' gives one-vs-rest MARKERS; a named level (e.g. 'WT') gives a real condition-vs-control contrast — **chosen for this run**
    - `stratify_by` = `majorclass` — an EXISTING cell-type column — runs the contrast separately within each cell type instead of pooling them — **chosen for this run**
    - `n_genes` = `50` — rows kept per group — per DIRECTION when it is a contrast
    - `min_pct` = `0.1` — a gene must be detected in at least this fraction of the cells of one of the two populations compared, or it is not tested at all (Seurat FindMarkers' min.pct). Without it most genes enter the test undetected — on the DDX41 retina object 2/3 did — which triples the BH denominator and floods the ranking with divide-by-zero fold-changes above 2^20. 0 disables
    - `lfc` = `0.25` — minimum |log2 fold-change| for calling a gene significant — applied together with `padj`, and drawn as the volcano's vertical line. 0.25 is the single-cell convention (Seurat's FindMarkers threshold); 1.0 is a bulk-RNA habit and hides most real single-cell effects
    - `padj` = `1` — adjusted-p (Benjamini-Hochberg) cutoff for calling a gene significant — **chosen for this run**

**4. `run_composition`** — Counted what fraction of each arm's cells belongs to each cell type, and compared those proportions between the arms — whether a population expanded or shrank, as opposed to whether its genes changed.

**5. `run_clustering`** — Reduced the expression matrix to its main axes of variation, built a neighbourhood graph over the cells, and grouped them into clusters, then laid the cells out on a 2-D UMAP map for display. Only needed when the data does not already carry cell-type labels.

    - `select_resolution` = `True` — choose the resolution by bootstrap stability instead of accepting the default — **chosen for this run**
    - `n_bootstrap` = `10` — resampling rounds per candidate resolution when selecting one
    - `stability_min` = `0.9` — minimum adjusted Rand index a resolution must clear to be called stable
    - `n_pcs` = `30` — principal components fed into the neighbourhood graph
    - `n_neighbors` = `15` — neighbours per cell in that graph — larger gives smoother, coarser structure

**6. `run_enrichment`** — Took the genes that came out of the comparison and asked which biological pathways and Gene Ontology terms they over-represent, tested against the set of genes actually measured in this experiment rather than a generic background.

    - `lfc` = `0.25` — minimum |log2 fold-change| a DE gene must clear to enter the test. Pairing an effect-size floor with the p-value cutoff is what keeps a list of thousands of barely-changed genes from returning only large generic terms; 0.25 is the single-cell convention
    - `padj` = `0.05` — adjusted-p cutoff a DE gene must clear to enter the test — the same Benjamini-Hochberg cutoff run_de applies
    - `top_n_genes` = `0` — optional cap on how many genes enter the over-representation test. 0 means no cap — use every gene passing the thresholds below, which is the standard way ORA is run. Set it only to deliberately shorten a very long list, and say that you did
    - `top_n_terms` = `10` — how many enriched terms to report per group

**7. `run_gsea_prerank`** — Ranked every tested gene by its effect and asked which pathways are shifted toward the top or the bottom of that ranking — a whole-ranking view, complementary to enrichment on a cut list.

## Results

### Quality control and dataset composition
All 15,307 cells passed quality control filters (≥200 genes per cell, ≤10% mitochondrial reads, ≥3 cells per gene), and 22,387 genes were retained for analysis. The dataset comprised 11 major retinal cell classes, with rod photoreceptors dominating (10,057 cells), followed by bipolar cells (2,509), Müller glia (1,322), amacrine cells (650), and cones (611). Rare populations included microglia (84), endothelial cells (34), horizontal cells (16), retinal ganglion cells (14), pericytes (6), and retinal pigment epithelium (4). All cells were classified as singlets by DoubletFinder. Quality control metrics showed comparable mitochondrial fractions between conditions (WT: 1.60%, DDX41: 1.50%), with higher mean gene detection in DDX41 cells (2,076 vs 1,505 genes per cell), consistent with the transcriptional activation observed downstream.

![Figure 1. Quality control metrics for the single-cell RNA-seq dataset. Violin plots show the distribution of the number of genes detected per cell, total UMI counts, and percent mitochondrial reads for WT and DDX41 conditions.](figures/violin_qc_violin.png)

![Figure 2. Scatter plots of quality control metrics. Left: number of genes detected versus total UMI counts, colored by condition. Right: percent mitochondrial reads versus total UMI counts.](figures/scatter_qc_genes.png)

### Cell composition shifts
Comparison of cell-type proportions between DDX41 mutant and WT retinas revealed substantial remodeling (Table 1). Müller glia expanded from 5.91% to 12.57% of all cells (2.13-fold increase), and amacrine cells doubled from 2.85% to 6.26%. Conversely, cones were depleted 3.08-fold (5.52% to 1.79%), and bipolar cells declined from 18.88% to 12.80%. Rod proportions remained stable (66.02% vs 65.24%). Microglia showed a 3.62-fold relative increase but remained at low absolute abundance (0.27% to 0.96%). These shifts are descriptive only, as no statistical test is possible with one library per condition.

**Table 1. Cell composition by condition.**

| Major Class | WT (%) | DDX41 (%) | Fold Change (DDX41/WT) |
|-------------|--------|-----------|-------------------------|
| Rod         | 66.02  | 65.24     | 0.99                    |
| BC          | 18.88  | 12.80     | 0.68                    |
| MG          | 5.91   | 12.57     | 2.13                    |
| Cone        | 5.52   | 1.79      | 0.32                    |
| AC          | 2.85   | 6.26      | 2.20                    |

### Cell clustering and annotation stability
Leiden clustering at resolution 0.2 (bootstrap stability = 0.9605) produced 20 clusters that largely recapitulated known retinal cell types. Mapping these de novo clusters to the existing `majorclass` annotations confirmed that clusters corresponded to major classes with high purity: cluster 0 (99.9% rod), cluster 2 (99.6% Müller glia), cluster 3 (99.8% bipolar), and cluster 4 (100% cone). No novel, unannotated populations specific to the DDX41 mutant were detected. All downstream analyses used the pre-existing `majorclass` labels.

![Figure 3. UMAP embedding of 15,307 retinal cells colored by major class annotation (left) and sample condition (right). The embedding shows clear separation of major retinal cell types, with WT and DDX41 cells intermingled within each class.](figures/umap_majorclass_sampleid.png)

![Figure 4. UMAP embedding colored by Leiden cluster assignment at resolution 0.2 (20 clusters, stability = 0.9605). Clusters recapitulate known retinal cell types.](figures/umap_clusters.png)

### Per-cell-type transcriptional effect sizes

#### Müller glia exhibit reactive gliosis and translational activation
Müller glia exhibited the most dramatic transcriptional response of any cell class. The top up-regulated gene was *Gfap* (glial fibrillary acidic protein; log₂FC = +6.02, Wilcoxon score = 19.9), a canonical marker of reactive gliosis. Immune and complement genes were strongly induced, including *C4b* (log₂FC = +3.26), *Serping1* (log₂FC = +2.90), and *A2m* (log₂FC = +1.70). Down-regulated genes included synaptic receptors (*Grin2b*, log₂FC = −3.46; *Grin2d*, log₂FC = −3.18), consistent with synaptic remodeling and withdrawal from normal glial support functions.

Pathway over-representation analysis of up-regulated genes was dominated by translation-related terms, including Translation (R-HSA-72766), rRNA Processing (R-HSA-72312), and Macromolecule Biosynthetic Process (GO:0009059). Preranked GSEA confirmed this pattern, with Peptide Chain Elongation (R-HSA-156902; NES = +3.48, FDR < 0.0001) and Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842; NES = +3.48, FDR < 0.0001) as the top up-regulated pathways. Down-regulated pathways included Nervous System Development (GO:0007399), Cell-Cell Adhesion Via Plasma-Membrane Adhesion Molecules (GO:0098742), Axon Guidance (GO:0007411), and Synapse Assembly (GO:0007416).

![Figure 5. Volcano plot of transcriptional effect sizes in Müller glia. Log₂ fold-change (DDX41 vs WT) is plotted against Wilcoxon score. *Gfap* (log₂FC = +6.02) is the most strongly up-regulated gene.](figures/volcano_MG.png)

![Figure 6. Top enriched pathways among up-regulated genes in Müller glia by over-representation analysis. Translation and ribosome-related terms dominate.](figures/enrichment_MG_up.png)

![Figure 7. Top enriched pathways among down-regulated genes in Müller glia. Nervous system development and synaptic terms are suppressed.](figures/enrichment_MG_down.png)

#### Rod photoreceptors undergo extracellular matrix remodeling and metabolic suppression
Rods showed extreme up-regulation of extracellular matrix and injury-response genes, including *Col25a1* (log₂FC = +8.74), *Fgf2os* (log₂FC = +2.57), and *Fgf2* (log₂FC = +2.46). Down-regulated genes included axon guidance and synaptic molecules (*Dcc*, log₂FC = −5.83; *Nrn1*, log₂FC = −5.35; *Aplp2*, log₂FC = −4.91).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes identified Metabolism of RNA (R-HSA-8953854), Cellular Responses to Stress (R-HSA-2262752), and Translation (R-HSA-72766). Preranked GSEA revealed that Visual Phototransduction (R-HSA-2187338) was the most strongly down-regulated pathway (NES = −4.25, FDR < 0.0001), followed by Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856; NES = −4.12, FDR < 0.0001) and Hypoxia (NES = −3.33, FDR < 0.0001). Up-regulated pathways included Mitochondrial Electron Transport, NADH to Ubiquinone (GO:0006120; NES = +2.44, FDR < 0.0001) and Complex I Biogenesis (R-HSA-6799198; NES = +2.40, FDR < 0.0001).

![Figure 8. Volcano plot of transcriptional effect sizes in rod photoreceptors. *Col25a1* (log₂FC = +8.74) is the most strongly up-regulated gene, while *Dcc* (log₂FC = −5.83) is the most strongly down-regulated.](figures/volcano_Rod.png)

![Figure 9. Top enriched pathways among up-regulated genes in rods. RNA metabolism and translation terms are prominent.](figures/enrichment_Rod_up.png)

![Figure 10. Top enriched pathways among down-regulated genes in rods. Phototransduction and hypoxia pathways are suppressed.](figures/enrichment_Rod_down.png)

#### Cone photoreceptors activate a survival program with metabolic shift
Cones were overwhelmingly up-regulated, with 47 of the top 50 genes showing |log₂FC| ≥ 1.0. The strongest signal was *Cartpt* (cocaine- and amphetamine-regulated transcript peptide; log₂FC = +5.99). Down-regulated genes included ion channels (*Kcne2*, log₂FC = −2.11; *Kcnma1*).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes identified Oxidative Phosphorylation (MSigDB Hallmark) as the top term, along with Viral mRNA Translation (R-HSA-192823) and Translesion Synthesis pathways. Down-regulated genes were enriched for Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052), Pyruvate Metabolic Process (GO:0006090), Hypoxia, and mTORC1 Signaling. Preranked GSEA confirmed that Pyruvate Metabolic Process (GO:0006090; NES = −3.05, FDR < 0.0001), Carbohydrate Catabolic Process (GO:0016052; NES = −2.90, FDR < 0.0001), and Glycolytic Process (GO:0006096; NES = −2.87, FDR < 0.0001) were the most strongly down-regulated pathways. Visual Perception (GO:0007601) was also down-regulated (NES = −2.29, FDR = 0.004).

![Figure 11. Volcano plot of transcriptional effect sizes in cone photoreceptors. *Cartpt* (log₂FC = +5.99) is the most strongly up-regulated gene.](figures/volcano_Cone.png)

![Figure 12. Top enriched pathways among up-regulated genes in cones. Oxidative phosphorylation is the top term.](figures/enrichment_Cone_up.png)

![Figure 13. Top enriched pathways among down-regulated genes in cones. Glycolysis and pyruvate metabolism are suppressed.](figures/enrichment_Cone_down.png)

#### Bipolar cells show immune activation and phototransduction suppression
Bipolar cells showed strong immune and inflammatory up-regulation, including *Xlr3b* (log₂FC = +3.83), *A2m* (log₂FC = +3.32), and complement components (*C4b*, *Serping1*). Immediate-early genes were induced (*Fos*, log₂FC = +2.35; *Egr1*, log₂FC = +2.48; *Junb*, log₂FC = +1.98).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes was dominated by Translation (GO:0006412), Translation (R-HSA-72766), and Peptide Biosynthetic Process (GO:0043043). Down-regulated genes were enriched for Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856), Inactivation, Recovery and Regulation of Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514859), and Homophilic Cell Adhesion Via Plasma Membrane Adhesion Molecules (GO:0007156). Preranked GSEA identified Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856) as the top down-regulated pathway (NES = −2.67, FDR < 0.0001) and Viral mRNA Translation (R-HSA-192823) as the top up-regulated pathway (NES = +2.51, FDR < 0.0001).

![Figure 14. Volcano plot of transcriptional effect sizes in bipolar cells. *Xlr3b* (log₂FC = +3.83) and *A2m* (log₂FC = +3.32) are among the top up-regulated genes.](figures/volcano_BC.png)

![Figure 15. Top enriched pathways among up-regulated genes in bipolar cells. Translation-related terms dominate.](figures/enrichment_BC_up.png)

![Figure 16. Top enriched pathways among down-regulated genes in bipolar cells. Phototransduction cascade is the top term.](figures/enrichment_BC_down.png)

#### Amacrine cells suppress phototransduction genes and activate ribosomal stress
Amacrine cells showed massive down-regulation of phototransduction genes despite being non-photoreceptor interneurons: *Apoe* (log₂FC = −4.91), *Pde6g* (log₂FC = −1.90), *Rho* (log₂FC = −1.84), and *Gnat1* (log₂FC = −1.68). Up-regulated genes were heavily ribosomal and proteasomal (*Ubb*, *H3f3b*, *Rpl/Rps* family).

Pathway ORA of up-regulated genes identified Cytoplasmic Translation (GO:0002181), Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842), and Peptide Chain Elongation (R-HSA-156902). Down-regulated genes were enriched for Activation of Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2485179), Visual Phototransduction (R-HSA-2187338), and Phototransduction Cascade (R-HSA-2514856). Preranked GSEA confirmed that Eukaryotic Translation Elongation (R-HSA-156842) was the top up-regulated pathway (NES = +3.11, FDR < 0.0001), with 285 up-regulated and 24 down-regulated pathways significant at FDR < 0.05.

![Figure 17. Volcano plot of transcriptional effect sizes in amacrine cells. *Apoe* (log₂FC = −4.91) is the most strongly down-regulated gene.](figures/volcano_AC.png)

![Figure 18. Top enriched pathways among up-regulated genes in amacrine cells. Translation elongation and ribosomal terms dominate.](figures/enrichment_AC_up.png)

![Figure 19. Top enriched pathways among down-regulated genes in amacrine cells. Phototransduction cascade terms are prominent.](figures/enrichment_AC_down.png)

### Cross-cell-type synthesis reveals pan-retinal translational stress
The cross-cell-type analysis identified 1,715 genes up-regulated in at least two of the five tested classes with consensus direction. The top pan-retinal up-regulated genes included *Hmgn2* (consensus score = 0.664, detected in 5 of 5 classes), *Ubb* (consensus score = 0.660, 5/5 classes), *mt-Cytb* (consensus score = 0.575, 4/5 classes), and *Rps20* (consensus score = 0.486, 5/5 classes). These represent a shared translational and ribosomal stress response that transcends cell-type boundaries.

Cell-type-specific signatures included *Gfap* in Müller glia (log₂FC = +6.02), *Col25a1* in rods (log₂FC = +8.74), *Cartpt* in cones (log₂FC = +5.99), *Xlr3b* in bipolar cells (log₂FC = +3.83), and *Angpt1* in amacrine cells (log₂FC = +2.58). These genes represent cell-type-specific adaptations or degenerative markers that may serve as entry points for mechanistic studies.

## Discussion

This descriptive single-cell RNA-seq comparison of one DDX41 mutant and one WT retina reveals a complex landscape of transcriptional and cellular remodeling. Three dominant themes emerge, each generating testable hypotheses for future validation.

### Reactive gliosis as a central response to DDX41 loss
The most striking finding is the massive reactive gliosis in Müller glia, marked by a >6 log₂-fold induction of *Gfap* and complement activation (*C4b*, *Serping1*). This is accompanied by a doubling of the Müller glia population proportion, suggesting either proliferation, migration, or selective survival of glial cells. Reactive Müller gliosis is a hallmark of retinal injury and degeneration, and its prominence here suggests that DDX41 loss triggers a glial stress response that may be either cell-autonomous (DDX41 is required for glial quiescence) or non-cell-autonomous (glia respond to photoreceptor stress). The down-regulation of synaptic genes (*Grin2b*, *Grin2d*) and nervous system development pathways further suggests that reactive glia withdraw from their normal supportive functions, potentially exacerbating neuronal vulnerability.

### Pan-retinal translational stress
A translational and ribosomal stress signature was shared across all five tested cell classes. The top pan-retinal up-regulated genes (*Hmgn2*, *Ubb*, *Rps20*) and the dominance of translation-related pathways in ORA and GSEA (Eukaryotic Translation Elongation, Peptide Chain Elongation, Cytoplasmic Translation) point to a coordinated activation of the translational machinery. DDX41 is a DEAD-box helicase implicated in ribosome biogenesis and spliceosome function; its loss may directly impair ribosome assembly or mRNA processing, triggering a compensatory up-regulation of ribosomal protein genes and translation factors. This hypothesis is consistent with the known role of DDX41 in hematopoietic malignancies, where mutations lead to altered RNA splicing and ribosome dysfunction.

### Cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming
Cones and rods exhibited divergent metabolic responses. Cones up-regulated oxidative phosphorylation while suppressing glycolysis (down-regulation of Glycolytic Process, Pyruvate Metabolic Process, and Hypoxia pathways), suggesting a shift toward aerobic metabolism. This may represent a survival program, as cones also showed the strongest up-regulation of *Cartpt*, a neuropeptide associated with neuroprotection. Rods, in contrast, up-regulated extracellular matrix genes (*Col25a1*, *Fgf2*) and mitochondrial electron transport while suppressing phototransduction and glycolysis. The rod proportion remained stable despite these dramatic transcriptional changes, suggesting that rods are transcriptionally altered but not yet lost at this timepoint. The three-fold depletion of cones in the mutant, despite their apparent survival program, raises the possibility that cone loss occurs through a mechanism not captured by transcriptional profiling alone, such as cell death with rapid clearance.

## Limitations

1. **Absence of biological replicates.** Only one biological library exists per condition (WT: 1 donor, DDX41: 1 donor). All cells within a major class are subsamples of a single donor and thus pseudoreplicated. The Wilcoxon scores and log₂FC values reported here are descriptive, exploratory rank metrics only; they cannot be interpreted as inferential differential expression with valid p-values. No adjusted p-value or FDR cutoff was applied in the per-cell-type effect ranking.
2. **Untested cell classes.** Six of 11 major retinal classes (Endothelial, Horizontal, Microglia, Pericyte, Retinal Ganglion, RPE) could not be tested because they contained fewer than 30 cells in one or both conditions. The transcriptional state of these populations in the DDX41 mutant remains unknown.
3. **Descriptive composition analysis.** The cell composition shifts are descriptive only and cannot be statistically tested with one library per condition.
4. **Pathway enrichment as association.** All pathway enrichment results are associations with expression programs, not evidence of pathway activity or causation.
5. **Pre-annotated dataset.** The analysis was performed on a pre-annotated dataset; we did not perform de novo cell-type annotation or validate the existing labels.

## Conclusion
This descriptive single-cell comparison of one DDX41 mutant and one wild-type mouse retina identifies a triad of reactive Müller gliosis, pan-retinal translational stress, and cell-type-specific metabolic reprogramming as the dominant transcriptional responses to DDX41 loss. Cones exhibit a paradoxical survival program—up-regulating oxidative phosphorylation and *Cartpt*—despite their three-fold proportional depletion, while rods maintain population stability amid profound phototransduction suppression. These findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in independent biological replicates with orthogonal methods. If confirmed, they would position DDX41 as a critical regulator of retinal homeostasis and nominate it as a candidate gene for inherited retinal degenerations.

## Methods

1. **Quality control.** Cells were filtered using `run_scanpy_qc` with thresholds of ≥200 genes per cell, ≤10% mitochondrial reads, and ≥3 cells per gene. All 15,307 cells passed these filters (0 cells removed). After filtering, 22,387 genes were retained. The top 2,000 highly variable genes were selected using the `seurat_v3` flavor for downstream dimensionality reduction and clustering. Counts were normalized and log1p-transformed; raw counts were preserved in a `counts` layer.

2. **Dimensionality reduction and neighbor graph.** Principal component analysis was performed on the 2,000 highly variable genes, retaining 30 principal components. A k-nearest neighbor graph was constructed with 15 neighbors per cell using the PCA embedding.

3. **Clustering and resolution selection.** Leiden clustering was performed across a resolution sweep from 0.2 to 2.0. The optimal resolution was selected automatically by bootstrap stability analysis (`select_resolution=true`, `n_bootstrap=10`, `stability_min=0.9`). Resolution 0.2 was selected, yielding 20 clusters with a stability of 0.9605 (SD = 0.008). Cluster identities were reconciled against the pre-existing `majorclass` and `celltype` annotations.

4. **UMAP visualization.** A 2-D UMAP embedding was computed from the 30 principal components using 15 neighbors and a minimum distance of 0.3.

5. **Cell composition analysis.** The `run_composition` tool calculated the fraction of cells belonging to each `majorclass` per `sampleid`. Proportions are reported descriptively without statistical testing, as only one library exists per condition.

6. **Per-cell-type effect-size ranking.** The `run_de` tool was applied in contrast mode with `groupby='sampleid'` (reference = WT), stratified by `majorclass`. Within each major class, a Wilcoxon rank-sum test compared every DDX41 mutant cell against all WT cells, yielding per-gene log₂ fold-changes and Wilcoxon scores. Genes were required to be detected in at least 10% of cells in one population (`min_pct=0.1`), and a log₂FC threshold of 0.25 was applied. No adjusted p-value or FDR cutoff was applied; Wilcoxon scores are reported strictly as non-inferential rank metrics. The top 50 genes per direction (up and down) were retained per class. Five of 11 major classes met the minimum cell-number requirement (≥30 cells in both WT and DDX41 arms) and were tested: Rod (WT: 6,578, DDX41: 3,479), BC/Bipolar (WT: 1,197, DDX41: 1,312), MG/Müller Glia (WT: 803, DDX41: 519), AC/Amacrine (WT: 469, DDX41: 181), and Cone (WT: 310, DDX41: 301). Six classes were skipped due to insufficient cells: Endothelial, HC/Horizontal, Microglia, Pericyte, RGC/Retinal Ganglion, and RPE.

7. **Pathway over-representation analysis (ORA).** The `run_enrichment` tool performed over-representation analysis on the up- and down-regulated gene subsets per major class (genes with |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25) against three pathway libraries: GO Biological Process 2023, Reactome 2022, and MSigDB Hallmark 2020. The background was the set of all genes tested in this retina (11,293 genes). The top 10 enriched terms per subset were reported, ranked by adjusted p-value (Benjamini-Hochberg correction).

8. **Preranked gene-set enrichment analysis (GSEA).** The `run_gsea_prerank` tool performed preranked GSEA on the complete Wilcoxon-ranked gene lists (.rnk files) for each major class against the same three pathway libraries. Parameters included a minimum gene-set size of 15, maximum of 500, 1,000 permutations, and an FDR threshold of 0.05. Normalized Enrichment Scores (NES) and leading-edge genes were reported.

9. **Cross-cell-type synthesis.** The `run_code` tool aggregated the per-class DE tables, filtered for genes meeting the |log₂FC| ≥ 0.25 criterion, and computed a consensus ranking metric (|log₂FC| × fraction of cell types in which the gene was expressed) to identify genes changing consistently across multiple classes (pan-retinal signature) versus those restricted to specific cell types.
